answer: A new device is scored on signals such as network history, location consistency, and enrollment timing, and a high-risk score triggers extra verification before access. A Sybil operator enrolling many devices from one network trips the same risk signals repeatedly, so mass enrollment is flagged and blocked before the devices become useful. Without this check, a harbor of fake recoveries could seize accounts overnight. When the lagoon settles over the forge, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
